newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rains wash over key Brazil soybean regions - coops.
newsitem.headline: Rains wash over key Brazil soybean regions - coops.

text.p: Rains alleviated dryness in Brazil's key soybean growing region of Rio Grande do Sul but were holding up harvesting of the precocious cycle crop in Mato Grosso, growers said.

"Conditions are excellent," said Guiomar Backes, agronomist at the Coopermil cooperative in Santa Rosa. "It started raining yesterday and it's continuing. By 0800 local (1000 GMT) this morning we registered 92 mm."

"It started raining on Jan 29 and that improved the situation a little," said Marcos Ricardo Streck, agronomist at the Cotrican cooperative in Candelaria. "But there is already a crop loss of 10 to 20 percent for the precocious cycle crop."

"We are hoping for significant rains from today and during next week," Streck said. The medium-cycle crop, currently entering into the flowering phase, should suffer no losses providing it receives enough moisture, he added.
Growers said caterpillars remained a problem but it was mostly under control. Temperatures hovered in the high 20 degrees Celsius.
In Mato Grosso state, which traditionally starts harvesting in January, the harvest was suspended in some areas while growers waited for heavy rains to stop.

"We've had 15 days of strong rains," said Tony Fagundes at the Cooperlucas cooperative. "It's a very big concern but the forecasters tell us the weather should start clearing up from tomorrow so we're hopeful."
